front: When can the suvat equations be used?
back: Only for constant (uniform) acceleration in a straight line.

front: How are the suvat equations derived?
back: From a straight-line v-t graph: gradient = a gives v = u + at; area (trapezium) gives s = ½(u + v)t; eliminate v or t for the other two.
Motion under gravity alone (no air resistance), with acceleration g = 9.81 m s⁻² downwards.

front: Acceleration at the top of a vertical throw
back: Still 9.81 m s⁻² downwards; only the velocity is zero.

front: Braking distance from speed u with deceleration a

back: Thinking distance (speed × reaction time) + braking distance (u²/2a).

front: g from a graph of h against t²
back: From rest $h = \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2$: gradient $= g/2$, so $g = 2 \times$ gradient.

front: Ball thrown up, back at the launch level
back: Same speed as at launch, opposite direction (no air resistance).
